goal: Split individual fuzz target corpora into shards so runs can use multiple cores concurrently
Reduce overall fuzz test duration on CI and developer machines dominated by slow targets
reviewability: Ready for review despite draft status and ongoing performance evaluation
agreement: Concept support because splitting slow targets noticeably shortens MSan and Windows runs (jeanpablojp)
Resolved objection: coverage is reported per process, losing aggregate target comparisons (jeanpablojp)
Resolved objection: temp directory collisions and cleanup crashes on failed shards (jeanpablojp)

why: P3 because sharding cuts slow target tails, saving 7 to 15 minutes on Windows, ASan, and MSan CI runs
The runtime gains are partially reduced by extra per-input setup overhead and macOS disk IO costs

why: P3 because adding ramdisk and tmpfs mounts in CI runners mitigates disk contention during parallel fuzzing
The improvement is narrow and focused on reducing storage bottlenecks caused by corpus sharding
